card.name: Punctuation and linking words after noun phrases
card.fires_on: Commas, colons, periods and the word 'in' that come right after a complete noun phrase, often in quoted titles, citations and label sentences. The next words continue with a qualifier, subtitle or new clause.

modes.label: Comma after clause
modes.description: A comma ends a noun phrase and a trailing qualifier follows.

modes.label: Colon in book titles
modes.description: A colon separates the main title from its subtitle.
modes.example: one can start with Charles C. Mann’s twin volumes, 1491<<:>> New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus

modes.label: 'in' inside titles
modes.description: The word 'in' follows a title noun and introduces the topic or group.
modes.example: Highlights of the Report of the Expert Panel on Blood Cholesterol Levels<< in>> Children and Adolescents.
